title: Count vowels
instructorPromptText: Write a function that counts vowels in a string.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function count uppercase vowels (A, E, I, O, U) in addition to lowercase, or only one case?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Case handling is the most common unstated assumption in string-counting problems; forcing the student to commit surfaces whether they've thought about it.
English teaches 'y is sometimes a vowel'; this has no objectively correct answer, so the spec must commit to one.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the function return when given an empty string?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Empty input is the canonical missed case in CS1; surfacing it in the spec gate is cheaper than surfacing it in a failed test.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student's spec commits to counting uppercase vowels but code only checks lowercase because they wrote `if c in 'aeiou'` without .lower()
Spec commits to excluding 'y' but the student writes `'aeiouy'` in the check string by habit
Plan uses an accumulator variable and a for-loop; code uses `sum(1 for c in s if c.lower() in 'aeiou')` — coherent Pythonic refactor
Student initializes the counter inside the loop instead of before it, so the final count is always 0 or 1
Function computes the count correctly but prints it instead of returning it, so callers get None
